text:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (p99 > 2s). p95=420ms p99=2.6s error_rate=0.8% :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Auto-mitigation suggested: route-to-fallback-model=true, disable-prefix-cache-rollout for traffic-tag=canary

sara: seeing it on the dashboard. spike started ~2115011400 (about 18m ago). p99 climbed rapidly after 2115011200.
jay: i pushed the new prefix-hash change ~2115011000 as part of the caching rollout. rolling back now?

mike: copying in metrics: https://console.redwood.ai/slo/teams/infra/requests?range=1h (open if you need it)
olivia: streaming stall traces show long tail on stream write (client connection held open, kernel-level backpressure) - likely cache miss amplification
sara: traffic pattern: small prefixes get cold misses -> backend paging -> slow token generation -> stream stalls

jay: logs from router (snip):
```
2026-03-15T21:02:10Z router-5 debug route:get /v1/generate id=abc123 latency=2.45s cache_hit=false prefix_key=0x7e1a
2026-03-15T21:02:11Z shard-2 warn prefetch miss seq=256 kv_miss=true fetch_ms=780
```

mike: cache hitrate is tanking on prefix_cache: last 30m hit_rate=9% (baseline ~72%). eviction rate increased 12x after deploy
olivia: prefix hash entropy changed - new hash reduced prefix collision space; looks like higher collision -> more cache invalidations
sara: customer impact: a minority of requests (approx 0.7% of total) hit >2s and some streaming clients reported partial truncation due to timeouts. CS flagged 3 customers as impacted.

ops-bot: PagerDuty incident PDR-4723 created and assigned to oncall-sre
sara: i'm taking lead. @mike please coordinate rollback of the prefix-hash rollout. @jay can you prepare the PR revert?

jay: starting revert now. will pin to previous hash version and regradually rollout 0%->100% over 30m once warmup done.

mike: mitigation plan:
- rollback prefix-hash change to v20260218-hotfix (immediate) :heavy_check_mark:
- enable fallback-routing to compatibility model for 10% traffic (route flag)
- temporarily disable aggressive eviction policy on prefix_cache to 120s TTL
- manual warm-up: run synthetic warm requests against hot prefixes
- increase streaming request timeout at edge to 6s while warmup in progress

olivia: runbook commands:
```
# revert commit
git -C infra-cfg checkout v20260218-hotfix && deploy --env=prod --shards=all
# enable fallback
curl -XPOST https://controlplane.redwood.ai/flags -d '{"route_to_fallback":true,"pct":10}'
# check cache metrics
redis-cli -h prefix-cache-01 info | grep hit_rate
```

sara: i've notifed CS and product with a short incident message. tagging legal for customer-impact review (low latency degradation, no data exfiltration)

mike: rollback applied to 40% of shards at 2115012800. observing hit_rate improvement on those shards: +45% within 3m
jay: full rollback completed at 2115013600. running warm-up scripts now (batch of ~2000 prefix requests covering top-10k prefixes)

olivia: warm-up logs look good. global prefix_cache hit_rate climbing back to ~68% at 2115014200
sara: p99 decreased to 1.1s, p95=380ms. streaming stalls frequency down 80% from peak

incident-bot: NOTE: fallback flag still active (10%). Recommend keeping for 20m post-warmup.

mike: customer-impact summary for postmortem: ~0.7% of requests experienced >2s latency for ~1h window. 3 customers reported degraded streams; all recovered after warmup/rollback. No errors in model outputs. Cost impact: extra fallback routing + warmup ~estimated $1200.

sara: next steps / actions assigned:
- jay: post revert PR and postmortem section on rolling tests (assigned)
- olivia: add guard checks to hash rollout: simulate collision histogram and canary-level hit-rate checks (assigned)
- mike: improve runbook steps for manual warmup + add automated warmup job in infra (assigned)

jay: will add a preflight check to the rollout pipeline to prevent low-entropy hash configs from reaching prod

olivia: TL;DR for ops: bad prefix-hash change -> cache collision/invalidation spike -> paging + backend slowdowns -> streaming tail latency -> rollback + warmup mitigated.

sara: thanks team. I'll keep the incident open for postmortem drafting. moving to handoff -> oncall evening shift @mike will monitor for next 2 hours then hand back.

mike: monitoring. will @mention in 2h with status. :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation successful, SLO trending back to target. Incident will remain open for follow-up until postmortem is filed.
